entries.definition_en:
ἔκδικος, -ον
 (δίκη), [in LXX: Wis.12:12, Sir.30:6, 4Ma.15:29 * ;] 
__1. without law, unjust. 
 __2. exacting penalty from; as subst., an avenger: Rom.13:4; before περί, 1Th.4:6 (in π., a legal representative; Milligan, Th., l.with).†
 (AS)

ἐκ-καθαίρω 
 [in LXX for בָּעַר, etc. ;] 
__1. to cleanse thoroughly, cleanse out: with accusative, ἑαυτόν, 2Ti.2:21; of the impurity removed, ζυμήν, 1Co.5:7.† 
 (AS)

ἐκτός, 
 adv. [in LXX Jdg.8:26 20:15, 3Ki.10:13, al. (בַּד, Jdg.5:28 (בַּד), בַּד), Sng.4:1-3 (בַּד), al, ;] 
__1. as adv., outside, beyond: τὸ ἐ., with poss. genitive, the outside, Mat.23:26; in late Gk. (see Deiss., BS, 118), pleonastic, ἐκτός εἰ μή, 1Co.14:5 15:2, 1Ti.5:19. 
 __2. With force of prep., with genitive; 
 __(a) outside of: 1Co.6:18, 2Co.12:2; 
 __(b) beyond, besides, except: Act.26:22, 1Co.15:27.†
 (AS)

ἀκριβῶς 
 adv. (ἀκριβής), [in LXX: Deu.19:18 (יָטַב), Da TH 7:19 (יְצֵב), Eze.39:14, Wis.19:18, Sir.18:29 ;] 
with exactness, carefully: Mat.2:8, Luk.1:3, Act.18:25, Eph.5:15, 1Th.5:2 (M, Th., in l). Compar., ἀκριβέστερον (Milligan, NTD, 111; MM, VGT, see word), Act.18:26 23:15, 20 24:22.†
 (AS)

εὐλογέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX chiefly for בָּרַךְ pi. ;] 
__1. to speak well of, praise (cl.; LXX Deu.8:10, al.): τ. θεόν, Luk.1:64 2:28 24:51, 53 (αἰνοῦντες, T, WH, mg.), Jas.3:9; absol., to give praise, Mat.14:19 26:26 (see Swete on Mrk.14:22), Mrk.6:41 14:22 (see Swete, in l), Luk.24:30, 1Co.14:16. 
 __2. As in LXX (= בָּרַךְ pi.); 
 __(a) to bless, invoke blessings on (Gen.24:60, Num.23:20, al.): absol., 1Co.4:12, 1Pe.3:9; with accusative of person(s), Luk.2:34 6:28 24:50-51, Rom.12:14, Heb.7:1, 6-7 11:20-21; εὐλογημένος (= בָּרַךְ; see Lft., Notes, 310; DCG, i, 189), blessed, Mat.21:9 23:39" (LXX), Mrk.11:9-10, Luk.13:35 19:38" (LXX), Jhn.12:13; with accusative of thing(s), Mrk.8:7, Luk.9:16, 1Co.10:16; 
 __(b) with God as subject (Psa.44:3, al.), to bless, prosper, bestow blessings on: with accusative of person(s), Act.3:26, Gal.3:9, Eph.1:3 (Lft., Notes, 311), Heb.6:14; εὐλογημένος, Luk.1:28 (WH, tit., R, tit., omit) Luk.1:42; εὐλογημένοι τ. πατρός (cf. Isa.61:9), Mat.25:34; pass. Act.3:25 (cf. ἐν-, κατ-ευλογέω).†
 SYN.: see: αἰνέω, and cf. DCG, i, 189, 211; Cremer, 766 (AS)

Ἰλλυρικόν, -οῦ, τό 
 Illyricum, a region bordering on the Adriatic Sea: Rom.15:19.†
 (AS)

Ἰορδάνης, -ου, ὁ (Heb. יַרְדֵּן), 
 the Jordan: Mat.3:5, Mrk.1:5, al 
 (AS)

κατα-φιλέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX chiefly for נָשַׁק ;] 
to kiss fervently, kiss affectionately: Mat.26:49, Mrk.14:45, Luk.7:38, 45 15:20, Act.20:37.†
 (AS)

κοινωνός, -ή, -όν
 (κοινός), [in LXX: Pro.28:24, Isa.1:23 (חָבֵר), Mal.2:14 (חֲבֶרֶת), Est.8:13, al. ;] 
__1. as adj., = κοινός. 
 __2. As subst., ὁ, ἡ κ., 
 __(a) a partner, associate, companion: 2Co.8:23, Phm 17; with dative of person(s), Luk.5:10; with genitive of person(s), Heb.10:33; id. before ἐν, Mat.23:30; 
 __(b) a partaker, sharer: with genitive of thing(s), 1Co.10:18 10:20, 2Co.1:7, 1Pe.5:1, 2Pe.1:4 (see Deiss., BS, 368 n2).†
 (AS)

μέθη, -ης, ἡ 
 [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכַר and cognate forms ;] 
drunkenness: Luk.21:34; pl., Rom.13:13, Gal.5:21 †
 SYN.: see: κῶμος (AS)

Ναζαρηνός, -οῦ, ὁ 
 (on the Semitic form, see Dalman, Gr., 141 n.) 
a Nazarene: Mrk.1:24 10:47 14:67 16:6, Luk.4:34 24:19.†
 (AS)

νοιεω νοέω, -ῶ 
 (νοῦς), [in LXX chiefly for בִּין, also for שָׂכַל hi., etc ;] 
__1. to perceive with the mind, understand (for the phrase νοῶν κ. φρονῶν, in wills, see MM, xvii): absol., Mat.16:9, Mrk.8:17; with accusative, Eph.3:4, 1Ti.1:7; with dative instr., τ. καρδίᾳ, Jhn.12:40; pass., Rom.1:20; before ὅτι, Mat.15:17 16:11, Mrk.7:18; with accusative and inf., Heb.11:8. 
 __2. to think, consider: absol., Mat.24:15, Mrk.13:14, Eph.3:20; with accusative of thing(s), 2Ti.2:7 
 (cf. -εὐ, κατα-, μετα-, προ-, ὑπο-νοέω).†
 (AS)

Πέργαμος, -ου, ἡ
 (so Xen., Paus., al., but -ον, τό in Strabo, Polyb., and most writers, also in Inscr.; in NT the termination is uncertain) 
Pergamum, a city of Mysia: Rev.1:11 2:12.†
 (AS)

ἀνθρωποκτόνος, -ον
 (κτείνω, to kill) 
a murderer, manslayer (Eur.; see MM, VGT, see word): Jhn.8:44, 1Jn.3:16.† 
 SYN.: φονεύς, ἀνδροφόνος (see Tr., Syn, § 83) (AS)
a fold or pucker in the face, a wrinkle , Lat. ruga, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

σπήλαιον, -ου, τό 
 [in LXX chiefly for מְעָרָה ;] 
a cave, cavern: Jhn.11:38, Heb.11:38, Heb.6:15; σ. (EV, den) λῃστῶν (Jhn.7:11), Mat.21:13, Mrk.11:17, Luk.19:46.†
 (AS)

συνετός, ή, -όν
 (συνίημι), [in LXX for בִּין, חָכָם, etc. ;] 
intelligent, sagacious, understanding: Mat.11:25, Luk.10:21, Act.13:7, 1Co.1:19" (LXX) .†
 (AS)

χράω, κίχρημι 
 [in LXX for לָוָה, etc. ;] 
to lend: Luk.11:5.†
 (AS)

ἀπο-σπάω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX for נָתַק: ni., hi., etc. ;] 
to draw off or away, tear away (MM, see word): Act.20:30; μάχαιραν, draw a sword, Mat.26:51; pass., to be parted or withdrawn (Field, Notes, 134; but see Thayer, see word), Luk.22:41, Act.21:1.†
 (AS)

ἀσωτία, -ας, ή
 (ἀ- neg., σώζω), [in LXX: Pro.28:7 (זָלַל), 2Ma.6:4 * ;] 
prodigality, wastefulness, profligacy: Eph.5:18, Tit.1:6, 1Pe.4:4 (MM, see word).†
 SYN.: ἀσέλγεια, q.v (AS)

αὐχμηρός, -ά, -όν
 (αὐχμός, drought); 
__1. dry 
 __2. squalid, dismal: 2Pe.1:19 (MM, see word).†
 (AS)
incorruption, uprightness , (New Testament) (ML)

Βαλάκ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. בָּלָק), 
 Balak; (Num.22:2): Rev.2:14.†
 (AS)

βασανιστής, -οῦ, ὁ (βασανίζω), 
 prop., a torturer; used of a gaoler, Mat.18:34.† 
 (AS)

βιόω, -ῶ 
 (βίος), [in LXX: Pro.7:2 9:6 (חיה), Job.29:18, Wis.4:4 א 1, 12:23, Sir.40:28, 4Ma.5:22 17:18 * ;] 
to spend life, to live: τ. χρόνον βιῶσαι (cl., more frequently 2 aor., -ναι), 1Pe.4:2 (cf. Jb, l.with).† 
 SYN.: ζάω (which see). (AS)

A man living at the time of Divided Monarchy, only mentioned at Jer.35.3; 
 son of: Jeremiah (H3414N)
 § Jaazaniah = "Jehovah hears"
1) a Judean, son of the Maachathite, a captain of the Judean forces who visited Gedaliah at Mizpah after Gedaliah had been appointed governor of Judah by Nebuchadnezzar
2) son of Shaphan, an elder of Israel in the days of Ezekiel
3) son of Azur, one of the princes of the people against whom Ezekiel was directed to prophesy
4) a Rechabite, son of Jeremiah the prophet
